title: InferLog: Accelerating LLM Inference for Online Log Parsing via ICL-oriented Prefix Caching
summary: InferLog is a framework for accelerating LLM-based online log parsing by maximising KV cache reuse across concurrent requests. Given a batch of raw log messages, each query is paired with 5 dynamically selected in-context learning (ICL) examples chosen by DPP diversity + kNN similarity on pre-computed embeddings. InferLog's PAIR module then reorders those examples to maximise shared prefix across concurrent requests, increasing the KV cache hit rate and thereby reducing p95 end-to-end latency and improving throughput — without changing the underlying log parser. A separate configuration tuning component (AttMAML + SMBO) finds optimal vLLM scheduling parameters for each workload.

This reproduction replaces the full pipeline with a single Claude Sonnet 4.6 call per log message using two prompt strategies: a black-box prompt (Prompt A) that describes only the output format (replace dynamic tokens with <*>), and an informed prompt (Prompt B) that provides a 5-step tokenisation and classification methodology. Both prompts use 3 static few-shot examples drawn from the HPC dataset. The paper's post-processing normalisation (correct_single_template) is applied to every LLM response before saving.

dataset.name: HPC (Loghub-2k)
dataset.description: 2000 log messages from an HPC system, part of the Loghub-2k benchmark. Each log has a raw Content field (input) and an EventTemplate field (ground truth). 46 unique templates. Average log message length: 24.9 characters (~6.2 tokens).
dataset.reason_for_choice: HPC has the shortest average log message in Loghub-2k (24.9 chars), making it the cheapest dataset to run. The full 2000-log evaluation costs ~$14.54, the lowest of all 16 Loghub-2k datasets. Running all 2000 logs is required for PTA, RTA, and GA to be meaningful.

definitions.PA: Parsing Accuracy — fraction of log messages whose predicted template exactly matches the ground truth.
definitions.PTA: Precision Template Accuracy — fraction of predicted template groups that exactly match an oracle group.
definitions.RTA: Recall Template Accuracy — fraction of oracle template groups that are exactly recovered.
definitions.GA: Grouping Accuracy — fraction of log messages that fall into a correctly grouped cluster.

metric.evaluation_note: All four metrics use content-based joining (log message text as key), not positional indexing. GA denominator = 2000 for a full run, matching the paper's hardcoded /2000. The paper's comparison baselines (Default vLLM, PC, PC-Tune, PC-Chunk, BatchLLM, DivLog, LILAC, LogBatcher) are compared ONLY on p95-latency and throughput — NOT on PA/PTA/RTA/GA. Table 2 compares the same underlying system (DivLog + Qwen2.5-14B) with and without PAIR reordering; it does not compare against external log parsers on accuracy.

original_result.note: From Table 2 of the paper (HPC row). Both columns use the same underlying parser (DivLog with Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, ascending ICL permutation). 'w/o InferLog' = no PAIR reordering (natural ICL order); 'w/ InferLog' = PAIR reordering for KV cache optimisation. The primary comparison for our study is 'w/o InferLog', as our pipeline also does no prefix-aware reordering.

our_result.structural_gap: Single LLM call with static 3-shot examples. No dynamic ICL selection (DPP + kNN), no PAIR prefix reordering, no iterative configuration tuning. Paper uses Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct locally via vLLM with 100 concurrent requests; our pipeline is sequential.
